issue.title: test_timed_out_summary_script_exits_on_sigterm_without_sigkill asserts elapsed < 2.0 against its own 2.0s SIGKILL grace, so it has no headroom under the full parallel lane
issue.description:
Discovered while landing epic sase-x7.2.1 (temporary offline migration kit). Reported as
a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP by phase agent sase-x7.2.1.2 on 2026-09-05, whose diff touched only
`src/sase/migration_kit/`, `src/sase/main/parser_migrate.py`,
`src/sase/main/migrate_handler.py` and their tests -- nothing under `src/sase/axe/`.

The test drives a real Python subprocess through the clan-summary timeout path and then
asserts a hard wall-clock ceiling that is equal to its own SIGKILL grace, leaving zero
headroom under load:

- `CLAN_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is monkeypatched to `0.4`
- `CLAN_SUMMARY_KILL_GRACE_SECONDS` is monkeypatched to `2.0`
- the script installs a `SIGTERM` handler that exits 0, then sleeps 30s
- the test asserts `signal.SIGKILL not in signals` **and** `elapsed < 2.0`
  (`tests/test_clan_summary_script_execution.py:248-250`)

Under a heavily loaded parallel run, interpreter startup plus SIGTERM delivery and
handler scheduling can consume most of the 2.0s grace. Either the grace expires and a
real `SIGKILL` is sent (failing line 249), or the handled exit lands just past the
budget (failing line 250). Which of the two assertions actually tripped was not captured
in the original observation, so the exact failing line still needs to be confirmed.

Likely remedy: decouple the assertion from wall-clock -- assert the outcome
(`outcome: timeout` in the stderr artifact, `clan_summary` absent from meta) and the
absence of `SIGKILL`, and either drop the `elapsed` bound or give it real headroom above
`CLAN_SUMMARY_KILL_GRACE_SECONDS` instead of pinning it to exactly that value.

Same class as sase-uz (`test_chops_run_concurrently` asserting a fixed 1.8-second
host-speed ceiling).

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed once during a ~39,000-test parallel run on 2026-09-05 (phase agent sase-x7.2.1.2, unrelated migration-kit diff). Passed 4/4 on immediate isolated reruns of the same node on the same unchanged tree, so it is parallel/load-sensitive and does not reproduce serially. Re-verified serially on 2026-09-06 at master 16153bf56 by sase-x7.2.1.land: tests/test_clan_summary_script_execution.py passes 9/9 in isolation. Fail rate under load is uncharacterized (1 fail / 5+ passes observed).

payload.description: same root cause class: a test asserting a fixed absolute wall-clock ceiling that host contention can exceed

evidence.note: Independent reproduction on 2026-09-06: during unrelated commit-finalizer retry-loop verification, just check escalated to the governed full lane (core-identity-changed) and failed tests/test_clan_summary_script_execution.py::test_timed_out_summary_script_exits_on_sigterm_without_sigkill once. The local diff touched finalizer code/tests, not clan summary handling. Immediate unchanged rerun of both failed nodes with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q passed: 2 passed in 5.39s. This corroborates full-parallel/load sensitivity rather than a deterministic break.

Independent evidence proposed by phase sase-xq.3: during unrelated bead projection determinism verification on 2026-09-06, just check failed once at tests/test_clan_summary_script_execution.py::test_timed_out_summary_script_exits_on_sigterm_without_sigkill, and the exact test passed on the immediate unchanged rerun. The phase changed core dependency/finalizer-adjacent build files, not clan-summary timeout handling. This is the same full-lane/pass-on-rerun failure and zero-headroom wall-clock root cause already tracked here.

CI repair verification at 09c93253d on 2026-09-07: just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake still reports this task's node(s) above the baseline after the full 14-worker test-cost run passed all of them (38948 passed, one unrelated contract-manifest collection-format failure caused by the retry's PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-v). Re-evaluating the gate with only records predating family 019 (before 2026-09-07T01:57:19Z) still reports these node(s), proving this gate impact predates the CI fix. This is independent historical gate-impact evidence, not a fresh failure of the node. No baseline suppression was added.

Independent reproduction during fleet UI implementation verification on 2026-09-07: after lint/SASE validation passed, just check escalated to the governed full lane because the diff touched Justfile and config schema assets, then failed exactly tests/test_clan_summary_script_execution.py::test_timed_out_summary_script_exits_on_sigterm_without_sigkill. Immediate unchanged reruns of the exact node passed serially and under xdist -n4. The fleet UI diff touches dispatch federation, ACE Agents UI, keymaps, schema, and related tests; it does not touch clan-summary timeout handling. This corroborates the existing full-lane/load-sensitive zero-headroom wall-clock flake.

Independent reproduction during the sase-xe landing (workspace clone, master + landing integration changes, 2026-09-07): test_timed_out_summary_script_exits_on_sigterm_without_sigkill failed under just check's escalated full parallel lane (39399 passed / 6 failed) and passed immediately in isolation (1 passed in 3.06s). Same shape as the bead: the elapsed < 2.0 assertion has no headroom against the 2.0s SIGKILL grace under full parallel load.
